title: The Remedy Worse Than the Risk
input_data:
Authentication log for a high-privilege admin account:

09:02:18  auth-ad    Login FAILURE for account db-admin from workstation W-014 (office floor, known device)
09:02:20  auth-ad    Login FAILURE for account db-admin from workstation W-014 (office floor, known device)
09:02:23  auth-ad    Login FAILURE for account db-admin from workstation W-014 (office floor, known device)
09:02:41  auth-ad    Login SUCCESS for account db-admin from workstation W-014

Three failed attempts from the admin's own known workstation, then a success. No other account, no other source, no lateral movement, no data access.
ai_output: Credential compromise. Account db-admin experienced failed logins and is at risk. Recommended action: disable all administrator access immediately, wipe and reimage the workstation, revoke every active session across the fleet, and declare a full incident.
ground_truth: Likely a typo. Three failed attempts from the admin's own known workstation followed by a success is the shape of a mistyped password, not a compromise. The evidence cannot justify wiping a machine and disabling admin access, actions that would stop critical database operations across the company. The recommendation itself is the biggest risk in the alert.
explanation: The model produced a confident, dramatic recommendation from weak evidence. It confused 'possible' with 'confirmed' and turned a typo into a fleet-wide response. The failure is not just a wrong label; it is an unsafe action recommendation that creates a self-inflicted outage far worse than the event it claims to fix.
security_impact: Following the recommendation disables the database admin team, wipes a clean workstation, and revokes sessions while critical systems run unmanaged. The remedy is more damaging than the risk it targets, and it also diverts the response team from anything real.
recommended_validation: Before executing any recommended action, confirm it is proportionate to the evidence. Map the suggested response to the actual indicators, and force a human approval gate on actions that disrupt services, wipe machines, or revoke access.

possible_mitigations.name: Proportionality check
possible_mitigations.description: Match every recommended action to the evidence that supports it, and reject actions whose impact exceeds the confirmed threat.

possible_mitigations.name: Human gate on disruptive actions
possible_mitigations.description: Require a human approver before any recommendation that disables access, wipes a system, or revokes sessions.

possible_mitigations.name: Typo awareness
possible_mitigations.description: Recognize that a small number of failed logins from a known device followed by success is a common user typo.

possible_mitigations.name: Constrained recommendation catalog
possible_mitigations.description: Allow the model to choose only from a catalog of pre-vetted, proportional response actions.

learning_objective: An unsafe recommendation can do more damage than the attack it claims to stop. AI output is not just 'right or wrong'; it can be wrong in a way that actively harms. Validate proportionality before executing any recommended action.
teaching_points: Three failed logins from a known device followed by success is usually a typo.
A recommendation that disables a team is a bigger risk than the event it targets.
Map every recommended action to the evidence that supports it, and gate disruptive actions behind a human.
